_comment: The single source of truth for which of eblume's repos the `talos` bot
may touch, what lands in the agent pods' checkout pool (talos), and
which repos get the forge webhooks. Both halves read it:
grants -> reconciled onto the forge by `mise run forge-reconcile`
(.forgejo/workflows/forge-reconcile.yaml): every managed repo
gives the `talos` bot READ plus an owned fork `talos/<repo>`
(pod pool clones origin = talos/<repo>, upstream =
eblume/<repo> read-only). ONE FORK MODEL: the bot has write
on no repo — managed entries cannot declare write.
pool   -> read by the talos entrypoint's clone loop (default.nix in
eblume/talos) from the talos-repos ConfigMap at /etc/talos.
ALSO: every pool repo gets the forge->talos webhook (issue +
PR-review + PR open/close/merge/reopen triggers), reconciled
by the same task.
Entry: { "name": <repo>, "managed": true }
managed: true -> read grant + owned fork, as above. The marker
replaces the legacy `access`/`pool` fields; the
legacy shape is accepted until the cutover window
closes (drop-legacy follow-up after this flip).
Top-level `excluded`: [repo-name, ...] — eblume repos `talos` never
touches (archived, scratch, ...). Every eblume-owned NON-FORK repo
must appear either managed or excluded; `forge-reconcile --check`
fails on any repo in neither list (a coverage hole). eblume-owned
forks and other owners' repos are out of the scan.
Per-repo optional fields (managed shape):
release_hook: true  -> this repo also gets the forge->horkos release
webhook (push + tag-create + pull_request), reconciled
by the same task; the secret is the 'horkos forge
webhook' item in the blumeops vault, ESO-mounted on the
horkos pod. See eblume/horkos#17.
horkos_forge: true  -> the horkos-forge bot gets collaborator write
on this repo so horkos can post the settlement comment
on origin issues there; reconciled by the same task.
See eblume/horkos#40.
principals: {user: read|none}  -> grants a declared principal from
the top-level list read access on this repo.
Top-level `principals`: [user, ...] — the DECLARED set of extra
READ-ONLY principals (e.g. the `cli-agent` CLI principal; the forge
user must exist before it is listed). Every listed user is reconciled
against EVERY repo: a live grant on a repo with no per-repo entry is
revoked, so removing a principal's last per-repo entry means revoke.
Removing a principal from the list is a two-step demotion — first a
PR removing all its per-repo entries (the apply revokes), then a PR
dropping the list entry; the PR check fails a one-step demotion of a
granted principal. Per-repo `principals` keys must name a user from
this list; write is refused for them at load time. No write, no CI
trust — see docs/reference/infrastructure/cli-agent-forgejo-principal.md.
RECONCILE IS AUTHORITATIVE: a repo absent from both lists has its
`talos` collaboration REMOVED. Adding a repo means adding it here, not
clicking in the forge UI. See docs/reference/infrastructure/principals.md.
The managed shape forces read on every repo, which subsumes the
reconciler's PINNED_READ_ONLY invariant (agents, blumeops, horkos,
talos read-only on canonical): under it there is no way to declare a
write grant at all, so the deploy/release secrets those invariants
guard (horkos: ZOT_PUSH_API_KEY, RELEASE_FORGE_TOKEN; talos:
BLUMEOPS_CI_OP_TOKEN) stay out of agent reach by construction.
